commit.message:
fix: gate untrusted project extensions behind project trust

Creating session services for a repository loads and executes its
project-local extensions: the SDK's resource loader imports every
enabled .pi/extensions module (running its factory) and the session then
dispatches session_start handlers. Pi Web called createAgentSessionServices
without the SDK's project-trust resolver, so merely opening an untrusted
repository — via POST /api/agent/new or GET /api/models — ran
repository-controlled code locally, with no trust prompt (#236).

Add projectTrustReloadOptions(), which returns the SDK
resourceLoaderReloadOptions only when the project has trust-requiring
resources (hasTrustRequiringProjectResources) and resolves trust from the
ProjectTrustStore shared with the pi CLI, defaulting to untrusted. The
loader's pre-trust pass keeps project extensions out until the decision is
true, so untrusted repositories no longer auto-run their code while
projects already trusted via the CLI keep working. Wire it into both
session-creation paths (startRpcSession and the models route).

Pi Web has no in-app trust prompt yet; until it does, a project is trusted
by trusting it once in the pi CLI. Ordinary projects without .pi
extensions are unaffected.

Fixes #236

fix DNS rebinding bypass

commit.message:
fix: resolve `enabledModels` glob patterns for the model selector (#310)

* fix: resolve enabledModels globs for the model selector

The model selector filtered available models by comparing enabledModels
entries as literal strings, so a pattern like "my-gateway/*" matched
nothing and every model behind it disappeared from Pi Web while pi's TUI
still listed it.

Delegate scoping to the SDK's resolveModelScopeWithDiagnostics() through
lib/model-scope.ts so globs, fuzzy patterns, and :thinkingLevel suffixes
behave exactly like pi's --models flag. Patterns that match nothing are
now reported as modelScopeWarnings instead of silently shrinking the
list, and an empty resolution still falls back to all available models.

Fixes #307

* fix: consume model-scope diagnostics and honor thinking-level pins

Review follow-ups on the enabledModels glob fix:

- Carry the `:thinkingLevel` pin through. The resolver returns
  `{ model, thinkingLevel }` for a pattern like `anthropic/*:high`, but only
  the model survived, so a new session still started at auto. `/api/models`
  now returns `thinkingLevelPins` and `useAgentSession` applies the pin of the
  model a new session starts with — the same rule as pi's buildSessionOptions.
- Give `modelScopeWarnings` a consumer: `ModelScopeWarningBanner` renders them
  above the composer, so a pattern that matched nothing is visible instead of
  silently shrinking the list.
- Drop the resolver catch-all. It could only fire when `getAvailable()` itself
  throws, which the route already handles, and it turned a real SDK fault into
  a silently unfiltered model list. The test that manufactured the throw by
  breaking an array iterator goes with it.
- Simplify `resolveVisibleModels`: take `ModelRuntime` and return pi's own
  `Model` type, removing the generic parameter, the structural runtime type and
  both `unknown` casts. `getAvailable()` is no longer called on the happy path.

* fix: apply enabled model scope at session startup

---------

Co-authored-by: Alex Yang <agegcn@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix: list dual-auth providers (Anthropic, Copilot, Codex) in the Models panel (#311)

* fix: list dual-auth providers in the Models panel

Anthropic was skipped by /api/auth/all-providers as "OAuth only" and by
/api/auth/providers through a hardcoded EXCLUDED set, so a configured
Anthropic account showed up in neither provider list even though its
models were selectable in chat. The same gap hid github-copilot and
openai-codex whenever they held an API-key credential, and there was no
way to add, rotate, or remove those keys from the UI.

Replace both id-based skip lists with capability-driven listing in
lib/provider-listing.ts: a provider is offered for API-key auth when it
declares auth.apiKey.login, for OAuth when it declares auth.oauth, and
its configured/loggedIn state now follows the stored credential type so a
dual-auth provider renders exactly once. Custom models.json providers
stay excluded (models_json_key and now models_json_command too) because
the panel already renders them from models.json.

Fixes #309

* fix: keep both provider lists in sync when the auth method changes

Review follow-ups on the dual-auth listing fix:

- Refresh both provider lists after any auth change. OAuth login reloaded only
  the OAuth list and saving an API key only the API-key list, so a dual-auth
  provider stayed rendered in its old list until the panel was reopened.
- Stop the stale row from deleting the new credential. auth.json holds one
  credential per provider and `logout()` removes whichever it is, so both delete
  routes now gate on `canRemoveCredential()` and return 409 when the stored
  credential belongs to the other method. Covers a second tab the refresh above
  cannot reach.
- openai-codex is OAuth-only in the pinned SDK — drop it from the dual-auth
  examples in AGENTS.md and lib/provider-listing.ts, and correct the test stub
  that claimed otherwise. Which providers declare both is an SDK property that
  moves between releases; the docs now say so instead of naming a fixed set.

* fix: make credential deletion atomic

---------

Co-authored-by: Peter Shi <peter.shi@zoom.us>
Co-authored-by: Alex Yang <agegcn@gmail.com>

fix: don't treat a single tilde as strikethrough (CJK ranges) (#392)

`~` is the standard CJK notation for numeric ranges (e.g. "5~7U",
"100~200倍"). GFM strikethrough accepts a single tilde as a delimiter, so
any assistant message with two `~` in one paragraph had the tildes
dropped and an arbitrary span struck through - silently corrupting the
content (a "5~7U" range renders as "57U"). This is common in LLM output
for CJK users.

Pass singleTilde:false to remark-gfm (its supported option) so
strikethrough requires ~~double~~ tildes, leaving single-tilde ranges
literal. Applied via the shared markdown plugin config, so chat, file
preview, and the minimap all honor it.

commit.message:
fix: don't misparse in-hunk diff lines as file headers (#394)

parseUnifiedPatch checked every line for a "--- "/"+++ " file header,
including lines inside a hunk body. A removed line whose content starts
with "-- " (raw line "--- ...") or an added line whose content starts
with "++ " (raw line "+++ ...") was therefore misread as a new file
header: flushChanges() ran mid-hunk and a bogus extra SplitDiffFile was
started, corrupting the split-diff view. This happens for ordinary
content — Markdown/reStructuredText bullets, and especially diffs that
themselves contain diff text.

Track the remaining line counts from the @@ hunk header (defaulting an
omitted count to 1) and only look for file headers when outside a hunk
body. Inside a hunk, "--- ..."/"+++ ..." lines fall through to the normal
-/+ content handling.

Adds regression tests for header-like in-hunk content and for resuming
header detection across multiple files.

commit.message:
fix: render YAML frontmatter as a metadata card in markdown preview (#391)

react-markdown has no frontmatter support, so a leading `---` block was
parsed as CommonMark instead: the opening `---` became an <hr> and the
closing `---` turned the YAML lines into a setext heading, leaking raw
metadata like `title: My Doc` into the rendered preview between two
horizontal rules (and letting remark-math mangle any $ inside it).

- Add remark-frontmatter (yaml only) to both render pipelines so the
  block parses as a `yaml` node and disappears from the rendered output.
- Add parseFrontmatter() (lib/markdown.ts) backed by js-yaml, and a
  FrontmatterCard that renders the metadata above the preview body:
  `title` as a heading, `tags`/`categories`/`keywords` as chips, remaining
  keys as a key/value table with http(s)/mailto values as links.
- Malformed YAML shows no card but is still hidden by the remark plugin;
  documents without frontmatter render exactly as before.

Verified with tsc --noEmit and eslint; the parse pipeline was also

commit.message:
fix: compare git-emitted paths correctly on Windows (#388)

* fix: compare git-emitted paths correctly on Windows

`git rev-parse --path-format=absolute` prints POSIX-style absolute paths
even on Windows (`D:/repo`), while `realpathSync()` and the session cwds
recorded by pi are native (`D:\repo`). `resolveProject()` compared the two
with `===`, so on Windows:

- `isTopLevel` was permanently false, which hid the worktree switcher
  entirely and left only the disabled "Open repo root" hint;
- `isWorktreeTopLevel` was therefore also always false, so linked
  worktrees never collapsed into the main repo's `projectRoot` and each
  showed up as a separate phantom project instead of being grouped;
- `listWorktrees()` returned slash-style paths that never matched
  `selectedCwd`, breaking the current-worktree highlight in the sidebar.

Route every path read out of git through `toNativePath()` and compare with
`samePath()`, which also tolerates drive-letter case since Windows paths
are case-insensitive. Branch names deliberately skip normalization so
`feature/x` does not become `feature\x`.

Both helpers live in a new `lib/paths.ts` alongside `isWindowsAbsolutePath()`,
which had been duplicated in `lib/file-access.ts` and `lib/path-security.ts`.
`isFilePathAllowed()` was a byte-for-byte copy of `isPathWithinRoots()` and
now delegates to it, leaving one implementation of the access-control check.
The allowed-roots set keeps its slash-normalized form: it is an internal Set
key that is never displayed, and containment checks re-normalize both sides
anyway, so both path forms authorize identically.

Verified on Windows against real repositories: repo roots now resolve as
top-level, subdirectories still do not, linked worktrees collapse to the
main repo, and `feature/x` keeps its slash. Adds `lib/paths.test.mjs`
covering separator style, drive-letter case and UNC paths.

commit.message:
fix: resolve hydration mismatch from browser extensions and responsive aria-valuemax (#463)

Two sources of hydration mismatch on initial page load:

1. Browser extensions (Grammarly, translation, password managers) mutate
   the <body> element's attributes before React hydrates. <html> already
   had suppressHydrationWarning but <body> did not.

2. The sidebar resize separator's aria-valuemax was computed via
   effectiveMaxWidth() during render, which calls getMaxWidth(). On the
   server this returns the constant maxWidth, but on the client it
   returns a viewport-dependent value, causing a mismatch for viewports
   between 641px and 799px wide. Gate the responsive computation behind
   a mounted flag so the initial render uses the constant maxWidth.

fix: suppress DEP0190 deprecation when auto-opening browser (#468)

* fix: suppress DEP0190 deprecation when auto-opening browser

Starting pi-web on Windows prints a Node.js DEP0190 deprecation warning:

  (node:XXXXX) [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child
  process with shell option true can lead to security vulnerabilities,
  as the arguments are not escaped, only concatenated.

This is emitted by the browser auto-open call, which used
`spawn(openCmd, [url], { shell: isWindows })`. DEP0190 triggers
whenever args are passed together with `shell: true`.

Refactor the call to avoid `shell: true` entirely while preserving
the same auto-open behavior:
- Windows: invoke `cmd.exe /c start "" <url>` directly so the URL
  is passed as a structured argv (the empty title is required by the
  `start` built-in).
- macOS / Linux: spawn `open` / `xdg-open` without `shell`.

* fix: validate browser launch port

fix: suppress DEP0190 deprecation when auto-opening browser (#468)

* fix: suppress DEP0190 deprecation when auto-opening browser

Starting pi-web on Windows prints a Node.js DEP0190 deprecation warning:

  (node:XXXXX) [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child
  process with shell option true can lead to security vulnerabilities,
  as the arguments are not escaped, only concatenated.

This is emitted by the browser auto-open call, which used
`spawn(openCmd, [url], { shell: isWindows })`. DEP0190 triggers
whenever args are passed together with `shell: true`.

Refactor the call to avoid `shell: true` entirely while preserving
the same auto-open behavior:
- Windows: invoke `cmd.exe /c start "" <url>` directly so the URL
  is passed as a structured argv (the empty title is required by the
  `start` built-in).
- macOS / Linux: spawn `open` / `xdg-open` without `shell`.

* fix: validate browser launch port

+
+**Host Runtime Environment**:

+# Isolate project command environments from the web host
+
+Pi Web sanitizes the environment of its built-in project shells instead of exposing the Next.js host runtime wholesale. The agent `bash` tool and direct user shell commands remove `PORT`, `NODE_ENV`, and `NEXT_*` variables while preserving the SDK-managed PATH, Pi session metadata, and all other inherited values; explicit variables set by a project command still take effect. Third-party extensions retain control of their own tools and subprocesses so existing overrides and remote execution integrations are not intercepted.

@@ -0,0 +1,172 @@ +# Internationalization + +Pi Web's interface uses a small internal i18n layer. It is intentionally kept +inside the application instead of introducing another runtime dependency, so +the UI can support more languages without coupling the server, API responses, +or Pi's own output to a particular language. + +## Current Languages + +The built-in language packages are: + +- `en` - English +- `zh-CN` - Simplified Chinese + +The initial locale is inferred from the browser. Users can change the locale +from the language control in the top bar. The selected locale is persisted in +`localStorage` under `pi-locale`. + +## Using Translations In A Component + +Client components should get the translation function from `useI18n`: + +```tsx +import { useI18n } from "@/hooks/useI18n"; + +export function ExampleButton() { + const { t } = useI18n(); + + return ; +} +``` + +The component must be rendered below `I18nProvider`. The application root +already provides it in `app/page.tsx`. + +Use parameters for values that change at runtime instead of concatenating +translated fragments: + +```tsx +{t("session.messageCount", { count: messageCount })} +``` + +The corresponding message can use `{count}`: + +```ts +"session.messageCount": "{count} messages" +``` + +This keeps the sentence structure under the control of each language package. + +## Adding A New Language + +### 1. Create The Message File + +Add a file under `lib/i18n/messages/`, using a BCP 47-style identifier. For +example, a Japanese package would be `lib/i18n/messages/ja.ts`: + +```ts +import type { LocalePlugin } from "../types"; + +/** Pi Web Japanese language package. */ +export const jaLocale: LocalePlugin = { + id: "ja", + label: "日本語", + messages: { + "common.language": "言語", + // Add the rest of the shared keys here. + }, +}; +``` + +The message keys must remain stable and language-neutral. Copy the complete +key set from `lib/i18n/messages/en.ts` when starting a new package. Missing +keys fall back to English, but a complete package is preferred for a user +facing language. + +### 2. Register The Package + +Import and register the package in `lib/i18n/registry.ts`: + +```ts +import { jaLocale } from "./messages/ja"; + +registerLocale(jaLocale); +``` + +`LocalePlugin.id` must be unique and non-empty. The label is displayed in the +language selector. `getSupportedLocales()` automatically exposes registered +packages to the UI. + +### 3. Update Locale-Specific Types If Needed + +The built-in `Locale` type currently lists `en` and `zh-CN` for compile-time +safety. When adding a built-in language, update that union in +`lib/i18n/types.ts` and update any locale validation that intentionally lists +the built-in identifiers. + +### 4. Add Tests + +Extend `lib/i18n/registry.test.mjs` when browser-language detection or registry +behavior changes. Extend `lib/i18n/format.test.mjs` when interpolation or +locale-aware formatting changes. A new language should at minimum verify its +registry id and a representative translation. + +## Adding Or Changing UI Text + +1. Add a stable key to both `lib/i18n/messages/en.ts` and + `lib/i18n/messages/zh-CN.ts`. +2. Put keys under a feature namespace such as `chat.*`, `files.*`, + `settings.*`, or `common.*`. +3. Use `t("namespace.key")` in visible text, `title`, `aria-label`, and + `placeholder` values. +4. Use interpolation for counts, names, paths, and other runtime values. +5. Keep product names, model names, provider names, commands, file paths, + user content, tool output, and server-provided error details unchanged. +6. Do not translate an API error by matching its English text. Translate only + the local UI fallback around it. + +Keep established technical terms in English when translating them would make +the interface harder to map back to commands, configuration fields, or Pi +documentation. This includes terms such as `Agent`, `API Key`, `Provider`, +`Token`, `worktree`, `Diff`, `CWD`, `Shell`, `Git`, `HEAD`, `OAuth`, and +`Mermaid`; preserve their conventional casing. Translate the surrounding +actions and status text. Common concepts with clear localized forms, such as +model, plugin, skill, prompt, context, and cache, can remain localized. + +For example: + +```ts +// en.ts +"files.uploadedCount": "{count} uploaded" + +// zh-CN.ts +"files.uploadedCount": "已上传 {count} 个文件" +``` + +```tsx +{t("files.uploadedCount", { count: uploadedCount })} +``` + +If a key is missing from the selected language, the formatter first tries the +English package and finally returns the key itself. Missing keys also produce +a development warning, which makes incomplete translations visible during +development. + +## Verification + +Run the following commands from the repository root: + +```bash +node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit +npm run lint +node_modules/.bin/jiti lib/i18n/registry.test.mjs +node_modules/.bin/jiti lib/i18n/format.test.mjs +node --test lib/*.test.mjs +``` + +Do not run `next build` during normal development. See the repository +development notes for the reason. + +## Design Principles + +Pi Web is a user-facing web interface. Internationalization is therefore an +accessibility and usability feature: people should be able to understand and +operate the interface in a language they are comfortable with. Language +support should lower the barrier to using Pi Web, not be treated as a measure +of technical expertise or as a reason to exclude otherwise useful +contributions. + +The i18n layer is deliberately incremental. Contributors can add a language +or improve a small group of UI messages without rewriting API contracts, +changing Pi's output, or introducing a large translation framework.
